decision.summary: The run is well grounded. Its sources are genuine, its temporal handling is careful (post-event pages are labelled, and a living pre_event-dated page showing actual results was correctly excluded), and every Jev flag was dispositioned. I found no high-severity issue. The main warning is in the brief's Business drivers section: it reads JPM's equal expense and revenue growth as JPM 'reinvesting more' than its peers. That ignores management's evidence that the expense growth was largely revenue-linked pay, that margins rose, and that dollar operating leverage was positive, and it drops claim-163's caveat that the expense and revenue growth rates may not share a basis. One claim (claim-035) lost its 'Wholesale' scope when it was trimmed to its quote, so it now reads as firm-wide deposit outperformance. Smaller issues: the brief overstates Equities' share of the revenue spike, says underwriting deterioration was 'across the market' when Dimon said it was not across the board, and cites regulation only as an upside. claim-116 drops a hedge, and a labour-market conditioning statement on consumer credit was never extracted.
